summary: The July nonfarm payrolls report landed today, the first major data point after the Fed's 9-to-3 vote on July 29 to hold rates at 3.50–3.75%, its most divided decision since 2016. Wall Street had expected a gain of just 83,000 jobs, with economists watching labor force participation, wage growth, and job composition for broader clues.
tweet: July payrolls hit after the Fed's most divided rate decision since 2016 — a weak print cements the rate-cut trade; a hot one hands Warsh the green light to hike in September.
